blocking.section: Rate limiting / Per-Node ceiling; Response caching; Failure matrix
blocking.issue: Operators who build alerts from this document will query a label value that does not exist and will page on a state Observability says is not degraded. (1) The document gives the `ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` reason as `state_store_memory`, but the Observability catalog defines it as `memory`. (2) The document says any derived ceiling without a published Node count uses the full limit 'with a degraded metric'. Observability says file mode without a declared ceiling is not degraded, and it raises `node_count_unknown` only for derived ceilings in Control mode, Planned (M2). A file-mode Cluster would therefore show a permanent degraded state.
blocking.evidence: Doc line 373: "`ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` reasons are `size_limit`, `buffer_budget` and `state_store_memory`." Observability line 161: "| `ruralz_cache_store_skipped_total` | Counter | stores | `policy`, `reason` | size_limit, buffer_budget, memory |". Doc line 250: "else derived from N_published, the `HeartbeatReply` `clusterNodeCount`, else the full limit with a degraded metric." Doc line 470: "| No Node count yet | Derived ceiling | Full limit, degraded metric | Open | Declared ceiling |". Observability line 234: "File mode without a declared ceiling uses the full limit (pack 8.8), which is not degraded." Observability reason table: "| `node_count_unknown` | A derived Rate Limit ceiling lacks the published Node count; Planned (M2) |".
blocking.fix: Line 373: use reason `memory`, or agree one value with Observability so both documents print the same one. Line 250: "else, in Control mode, the full limit with degraded reason `node_count_unknown`; file mode without a declared ceiling uses the full limit and is not degraded (pack 8.8)." Line 470: make the same distinction (see L3-2 for the merged row). Keep the edits word-neutral: the body is at 4,990 of 5,000 words.

blocking.section: Failure matrix; Rate limiting / Per-Node ceiling
blocking.issue: Acceptance criterion 3 asks for fail-open or fail-closed behavior for each dependency failure. Ruralz Control is the second external dependency of the rate-limit path, since it publishes `clusterNodeCount`, but no row names its outage. The consequence also goes unstated. A Node keeps the count only in memory, and pack 8.11 lets a Node persist only its identity, Last-Known-Good and disposable caches. So a Node that restarts from Last-Known-Good while Ruralz Control is down has no count and uses the full limit as its ceiling. If the State Store is also failing, fail-open admission reaches about N x limit instead of the 2 x limit the document advertises. Separately, the 'Nodes lost' row gives a 60 s rule for small decreases that Control plane and GitOps no longer states, and the quoted counting rule at line 254 does not match the source text.
blocking.evidence: Doc line 254: "Nodes apply the value as received and keep it while Ruralz Control is down." Doc line 470: "| No Node count yet | Derived ceiling | Full limit, degraded metric | Open | Declared ceiling |" (no row names Ruralz Control). Pack 8.11: "A Node persists only the following under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`" (identity, Last-Known-Good, disposable caches). Doc line 471: "| Nodes lost | Derived ceiling | Large decreases publish at once, small ones after 60 s (target); keys under-admit meanwhile | Closed | No |". Control plane and GitOps line 115: "`clusterNodeCount` counts ready Nodes that ACKed a Revision and stayed connected 10 minutes (target); large decreases publish at once, and increases rise at most 10% per minute, with an alert (target)." Doc line 254 quotes it as "ready, streaming Nodes that ACKed a Revision and stayed connected 10 minutes (target)".
blocking.fix: Replace the line 470 row with: "| Ruralz Control unreachable, or no Node count yet | Derived ceiling | Keep the last count in memory; a Node restarted from Last-Known-Good has none and uses the full limit (`node_count_unknown`), so fail-open admits up to N x limit | Open | Declared ceiling; OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-19 |". Either accept that bound explicitly, or add an option to OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-19 that persists the last count under `${RURALZ_DATA_DIR}`, which is a pack 8.11 amendment. Line 471: "Large decreases publish at once ([Control plane and GitOps](04-control-plane-and-gitops.md#replica-roles)); keys under-admit until then". Line 254: quote the source sentence verbatim or paraphrase it without quotation marks.

blocking.section: Circuit breakers; Traffic shaping / KrakenD EE routing and traffic features
blocking.issue: The breaker opens only when both `consecutiveFailures` and a fixed ratio guard hold: 50% of at least 20 legs in 10 s, per Upstream per Node. So on any Node that sends fewer than 2 legs per second to an Upstream, the breaker can never open, whatever `consecutiveFailures` says. At 100 Nodes, an Upstream receiving under about 200 legs per second Cluster-wide is never broken. The document does not state this. It maps KrakenD's 'Customizable HTTP circuit breaker' to `circuitBreaker` as if equivalent, although KrakenD's breaker opens on consecutive errors alone (`max_errors`). An operator or a KrakenD migrant who sets `consecutiveFailures: 3` will expect behavior the design never produces, and no text tells them which mechanism protects low-traffic Upstreams instead.
blocking.evidence: Line 173: "| `consecutiveFailures` | Opens the breaker once that many consecutive legs failed and at least 50% of at least 20 legs in a rolling 10 s window (target) | 503 `RZ-UP-005` at once, no retry |". Line 179: "The guards are fixed until OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-5 adds fields." Line 442: "| Customizable HTTP circuit breaker | `circuitBreaker` with CEL `failureWhen` | Planned (M1) |". docs/_meta/research/krakend-config-model.md line 127: "`qos/circuit-breaker` | B | CE | Consecutive-error breaker (`interval`, `timeout`, `max_errors`, ...)" (https://www.krakend.io/docs/backends/circuit-breaker/).
blocking.fix: Add to Circuit breakers: "Below 20 legs per 10 s per Node the breaker never opens; passive ejection, the retry budget and `maxPendingRequests` protect such Upstreams." Make one of these two changes as well. (a) Let the volume floor fall back to `consecutiveFailures` alone when fewer than 20 legs arrive, and state the false-trip trade-off. (b) Keep the floor, mark `minimumLegs` in OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-5 as blocking for M1, and add to the KrakenD row that `max_errors` imports with fidelity `approximate`. Keep the change word-neutral.

non_blocking.suggestion: The body is 4,990 words by the verify-docs rule (fenced code excluded) against a 5,000 cap, so every fix must cut as many words as it adds. Candidate cuts: the second sentence of line 94 (Cluster-wide probe arithmetic); the 'Principal' row justification at line 354; the duplicated 'hot entry' arithmetic in the Failure matrix row at line 463, which restates line 370; and 'Pack 8.8 names a foundation pack section' at line 24.

Step 5 resends the script as `EVAL` on `NOSCRIPT` 'within the same deadline'. That is a second blocking round trip for one Policy, which pack 8.7 rule 1 forbids, although the Tech stack Rate limiting row endorses `EVALSHA` with `NOSCRIPT` fallback. Either send `EVAL` on the first call after a State client reconnect or failover, or list the exception in OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 as a pack 8.7 clarification.

Line 210 says 'This local admission amends pack 8.8', but OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-20 is still open. Write 'proposes to amend pack 8.8' so readers do not treat the local-only path as frozen.

State what non-probe attempts get while the breaker is half-open (presumably 503 `RZ-UP-005` at once). Figure 1's gate node 'Breaker closed and in-flight slot or pending room?' omits the half-open probe path.

A background revalidation that returns 200 is discarded ('any other result ends the stale window, unstored'), so the next request misses synchronously. RFC 5861 expects the fresh response to replace the entry. Add the reason, presumably that the replay skipped the Route's response Phases, so the response cannot be stored as clients would receive it. This keeps implementers from 'fixing' it.

Line 362 rejects `cache` combined with 'an `onRequestBody` authz' Policy. `authz.cel`, `authz.opa` and `authz.cedar` register both `onRequestHeaders` and `onRequestBody`, so say whether every such Policy counts, or only those whose rule reads `request.body`. Otherwise every Route with `authz.cel` may be unable to cache.

ac_results.ac: Rate limiting specifies the IETF RateLimit-Policy and RateLimit response header contract.
ac_results.note: Names draft-ietf-httpapi-ratelimit-headers-11 as an Internet-Draft and uses RFC 9651 Structured Field lists. It gives `q`, `w`, `r` and `t` per RZ-RL code and Retry-After precedence (as research quotes), explains why `pk` and `qu` are omitted, and includes a worked 429 example. Headers on admitted responses wait on OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-2 (blocking, M1), because the `ratelimit` type registers no response Phase. That gap is acceptable, but the contract is complete only for 429 responses.

ac_results.ac: Quotas supports long windows and token-weighted units, including LLM tokens.
ac_results.note: Fixed windows aligned to the Unix epoch in UTC (`24h`, `720h`). Units are `requests` through `quota` and `tokens` (LLM input plus output) through `ai.token-budget`, with the pack 8.9 reservation and settlement. The Consumer and Policy example uses only Configuration model fields. Calendar months and weighted costs go to OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-10.

ac_results.ac: Timeouts, deadlines, retries and hedging defines a retry budget.
ac_results.note: The 'Retry budget' H3 sets in-flight retries, backoff included, at most max(3, 20% of in-flight originals) per Upstream per Node (target). It adds a metric and an amplification bound of 1.2 times from 15 originals, which checks out arithmetically. Hedges count against the budget.

ac_results.ac: Response caching follows HTTP caching semantics including stale-while-revalidate.
ac_results.note: Covers RFC 9111 storability (including Authorization, `no-cache` not stored at M1, `private`, `Vary: *`), freshness order, stale limits (`must-revalidate`, `proxy-revalidate`, `s-maxage` per sections 4.2.4 and 5.2.2.10), request directives including `only-if-cached` 504, revalidation, invalidation (the RFC 9111 section 4.4 gap is in OQ-11), RFC 9211 Cache-Status, and RFC 5861 `stale-while-revalidate` and `stale-if-error` with a sequence diagram. The discarded 200 on revalidation needs a stated reason (non-blocking).

foundation_amendments: Pack 8.11: consider allowing a Node to persist the last received `clusterNodeCount` beside Last-Known-Good, so a Node restarted during a Ruralz Control outage keeps a derived Rate Limit ceiling instead of falling back to the full limit (see L3-2 and OQ-traffic-management-and-resilience-19).

Pack 8.7 rule 1: clarify whether a `NOSCRIPT` resend of the same script counts as the one blocking State Store round trip, since the Tech stack Rate limiting row endorses `EVALSHA` with `NOSCRIPT` fallback.
